mcqs.q: An impression tray is a device used to:
opts: Carry, confine and control the impression material while making an impression
Pour and store the final cast
mcqs.explain: The tray carries, confines and controls the impression material in the mouth.

mcqs.q: The three parts of an impression tray are the:
mcqs.explain: Tray parts: handle, flange and body.

mcqs.q: A water-cooled rim-lock tray is specifically used for which impression material?
mcqs.explain: Water-cooled rim-lock trays are for agar; non-water-cooled rim-lock trays are for alginate/RBIM.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a recommended method of sterilizing impression trays?
mcqs.explain: Trays are sterilized by autoclave, dry heat or chemical vapor; disposable trays are recommended.

mcqs.q: The five objectives of an impression are preservation, support, stability, esthetics and:
mcqs.explain: The objectives (P-S-S-E-R) are preservation, support, stability, esthetics and retention.

mcqs.q: Maximum coverage of the denture-bearing area provides the 'snowshoe effect', which mainly improves:
opts: Support (by distributing forces over the widest area)
mcqs.explain: Broad coverage spreads occlusal load over the tissues (snowshoe effect), aiding support (and thereby stability, retention and preservation).

mcqs.q: Excess pressure during the impression technique is undesirable because it leads to:
mcqs.explain: Pressure recorded in the impression becomes denture pressure, damaging soft tissue and resorbing bone (poor preservation).

opts: Loss of vertical ridge height or an increase in flabby, movable tissue
mcqs.explain: Stability depends on close adaptation to firm mucosa; it falls as ridges resorb or flabby tissue increases.

mcqs.q: 'Adhesion' as a retention factor is the physical attraction of:
opts: Unlike molecules (saliva to the mucosa and the denture)
Like molecules within the saliva layer
mcqs.explain: Adhesion = attraction of unlike molecules (saliva–mucosa and saliva–denture); cohesion = attraction of like molecules within the saliva layer.

mcqs.q: For atmospheric pressure to aid denture retention, the denture must have:
opts: A perfect (effective) seal around its entire border
mcqs.explain: Atmospheric pressure resists dislodging forces only if there is a complete peripheral border seal.

mcqs.q: Which materials are commonly used for PRELIMINARY impressions?
mcqs.explain: Preliminary impressions use impression compound, alginate, or putty-consistency elastomers.

mcqs.q: Dental plaster (β-hemihydrate) and dental stone (α-hemihydrate) differ mainly in:
opts: Particle form/porosity, giving stone greater strength
Their chemical formula (one is not gypsum)
mcqs.explain: Both are calcium sulfate hemihydrate; α-hemihydrate (stone) has denser, less porous particles and is stronger than β (plaster).

mcqs.q: When mixing gypsum for a cast, you should:
opts: Add the powder to the water and spatulate 30–60 s, then vibrate to remove bubbles
Add water to a fully mixed powder
mcqs.explain: Add powder to measured water, spatulate 30–60 s and vibrate to reduce bubbles.

mcqs.q: The base of a poured cast should have a minimum thickness of about:
mcqs.explain: A cast base should be at least ~15–16 mm thick at its thinnest point for strength.

mcqs.q: The cast should be separated from the impression:
opts: About one hour after the initial set
mcqs.explain: Separate the cast about one hour after the initial set, then trim and finish.

saqs.q: Define an impression tray and list its parts and four ways of classifying trays.
saqs.a: An impression tray is a device used to carry, confine and control impression material while making an impression. Parts: handle, flange and body. Classifications: by material (metallic/non-metallic), extent (stock — full-arch/sectional/quadrant — or custom), dentition (edentulous/dentulous), and retention/design (perforated/non-perforated/rim-lock).

saqs.q: State the five objectives of an impression and briefly explain support.
saqs.a: Preservation, support, stability, esthetics and retention. Support is provided by maximum coverage of the denture-bearing area, giving the 'snowshoe effect' that distributes applied forces over as wide an area as possible; this in turn helps preservation, stability and retention.

saqs.q: List the five factors affecting denture retention.
saqs.a: 1) Adhesion (attraction of unlike molecules — saliva to mucosa and denture). 2) Cohesion (attraction of like molecules within the saliva layer). 3) Mechanical locking into undercuts (e.g. lateral tuberosities, maxillary premolar, distolingual and lingual mandibular premolar areas). 4) Atmospheric pressure (needs a perfect peripheral seal). 5) Muscle control and patient tolerance (a largely learned process).

saqs.q: Name the materials used for preliminary casts and describe how a cast is poured.
saqs.a: Preliminary casts are poured in β-hemihydrate (dental plaster) or α-hemihydrate (dental stone). Weigh the powder and measure the water; add powder to water and spatulate 30–60 s, then vibrate to remove bubbles. Dry excess water from the impression, hold it on a vibrator and let the mix flow from one end around the impression, fill it, and form the base (≥15–16 mm) using the extra material (inversion method). Separate the cast about one hour after the initial set, then trim and finish.

saqs.q: Why should the retractor rest on bone rather than on the flap, and how does a Seldin retractor differ from a periosteal elevator?
saqs.a: The retractor edge is placed on bone (not on the flap) so it does not put pressure/traction on the reflected soft tissue, protecting the flap while giving access and vision. The Seldin retractor may look like a periosteal elevator, but its leading edge is NOT sharp, so it is used only for retraction and must not be used to elevate the mucoperiosteum.
